text:
The Penguins ended a four-game winless run (0-3-1) in Los Angeles on a night when Tommy Novak, a 2015 fifth-round pick of the Predators who once played three games in the ECHL, scored twice in the first 5:10 and Sidney Crosby added two more. Crosby's second, a poke in the final minutes, made it 5-2.

By the numbers, the Kings were the better team. They attempted 71 shots to Pittsburgh's 50 and put 28 on net to PIT's 19. Their chances were worth 3.99 expected goals (a measure of shot quality) against 2.80 for the Penguins, and in our simulations of every shot, LAK wins this game 80 percent of the time. Corey Perry cut it to 2-1 in the first, and Alex Laferriere scored on the power play early in the second and took seven shots on goal. LAK's edge was greatest in the first period, 1.84 to 0.97 in expected goals, yet Egor Chinakhov made it 3-1 on a power play with 29 seconds left in the period, a goal that carried only a 6 percent chance.

The gap came down to goaltending. Sergei Murashov stopped 26 of 28 shots, about two goals better than the quality of those shots would predict. Darcy Kuemper allowed four goals on 18 shots, a bit worse than expected. Evgeni Malkin's three assists, and the line around him, gave Pittsburgh enough finishing to turn a lopsided game into a comfortable win. The Penguins leave with the winless run behind them. The Kings, who outplayed them and still lost, have little to say about the process and plenty to fix on the scoreboard.
